greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. We gather today in the peace of Christ, who invites us all to His eternal feast.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the shepherd who leads us to restful waters: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the host who prepares a table for us in the presence of our sorrows: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the way, the truth, and the life, who clothes us in the garment of your grace: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
homily:
We often imagine the Kingdom of God as a distant, abstract reality, a place we might reach only after a long and arduous journey through the clouds. But in our first reading today, the prophet Isaiah offers us a different, more tactile vision. He speaks of a mountain—a place of meeting—where the Lord of hosts provides a feast of rich food and choice wines. It is not a thin or ethereal experience. It is a banquet. It is abundance. It is the wiping away of every tear from every face. Isaiah tells us that on this mountain, the Lord will destroy the veil that covers all peoples, the web that is woven over the nations. He will destroy death forever.

Think for a moment about the image of a veil. It is a thin fabric, yet it is enough to obscure our vision. It is enough to make the world feel gray, to make the horizon seem unreachable, to make the present moment feel like an end rather than a beginning. We have all known that feeling of walking through a day with a veil over our eyes—when the light seems muted and the joy of the world feels like it belongs to someone else. We feel the weight of the web, the way our grief or our confusion can weave itself into our daily routines, making the path ahead look foggy and uncertain.

But the promise of the Gospel is that the King is throwing a wedding feast. He is not hosting a funeral; He is hosting a celebration. He is inviting us to a table that is already set. In the Gospel of Matthew, we see the King sending out his servants to gather everyone they find—the bad and the good alike. It is a radical, unsettling hospitality. It ignores our human categories of who is ‘worthy’ and who is not. It simply says: 'The feast is ready. Come.'

Benjamin Vo understood this invitation in his own quiet, brilliant way. You remember how he loved the precision of flight, the way a Boeing 737 would lift off the runway and pierce through the cloud layer into the clear, brilliant blue above. He loved the mechanics of it, yes, but he also loved the freedom of it. He was a boy who lived with his eyes toward the sky, always sensing that there was more to this life than what was immediately visible. He was a boy who lived as if the feast were already beginning. Whether he was coding a new application, dreaming up his 'con chim airlines,' or simply sitting with his family, there was a sense of purpose in him that transcended the smallness of the daily grind.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these three months, the silence of your home has been a heavy companion. You remember the way Ben would come down the stairs, always the first to offer a 'Good morning, Dad.' You remember the way he would listen to your stories—those made-up, joking stories—with such rapt attention, as if they were the most important truths in the world. That was his gift to you. He was a boy who knew how to honor the people he loved by truly listening to them. And that listening was a form of prayer. It was a way of saying, 'You matter to me.'

There is a profound comfort in what Jesus says today. He does not say that we are invited only if we are perfect. He says the hall was filled with guests. And yet, there is that one man without a wedding garment. It is a jarring moment in the parable. But consider what the wedding garment represents. It is not something we buy or sew ourselves. In the tradition of the Church, the wedding garment is the grace of Christ—the very life of God that is given to us, not earned by us. It is the grace that covers our nakedness, that warms us, that makes us fit for the banquet. When the King asks the man why he is not wearing it, he is silent. The man has no answer because he tried to enter on his own terms, in his own clothes, by his own strength.

We sometimes try to do the same. We try to carry our grief in our own strength. We try to be the 'strong ones' who do not need the garment of grace. We think that if we just grit our teeth, if we just keep moving, if we just stay busy, we can fix the emptiness. But the Gospel is telling us that we cannot fix this on our own. We need the garment. We need the grace that is provided by the King. We need to let ourselves be clothed in the mercy of God, especially when we feel most exposed, most vulnerable, and most empty.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the secret language of that love. You know that Ben is not gone; he has simply gone ahead to the place where all the 'con chim airlines' finally take flight. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity, his kindness, and his smile. When you sit down to code, or when you look up at the clouds, know that you are not doing it alone. You are a family of four, and that bond is stronger than death. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the brother who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share. You are a witness to the fact that love is the only thing that actually lasts.

I want to speak for a moment to the weight that can sometimes settle on the heart, the quiet questioning that happens when we are alone. Sometimes, we look back and we wonder if we could have done more, if we could have seen more, if we could have changed the path. I want to tell you, as clearly as I can: you were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his world, and he was yours. God does not look at your love and find it insufficient. He does not look at your past and find it faulty. You are not being asked to carry the weight of the past; you are being asked to walk into the future with the promise of the Resurrection as your light. Let that stone of self-reproach fall. It is not yours to carry. You are not being accused by God; you are being embraced by Him.

Saint Paul tells us in the second reading, 'I can do all things in him who strengthens me.' He says this after having known both abundance and need. He has learned the secret of contentment. It is not that he has everything he wants; it is that he has the One who is everything. That is the secret Benjamin knew. He knew that even when the world is confusing, even when the plans we make don't go the way we expected, there is a King who is preparing a table. There is a King who is wiping away the tears.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what you are doing. You are taking the love that was poured into Ben, and you are letting it flow into the lives of others. You are ensuring that his life is not a closed chapter, but a living, breathing, life-sustaining force. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to forgive, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

Do not be afraid of the silence, and do not be afraid of the ache. That ache is simply your love looking for a place to land. Let it land on the promise of the Resurrection. Let it land on the certainty that Benjamin is not in the past; he is in the future. He is at the destination, waiting for you to complete the journey. He is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that the King has prepared a feast for you, and your seat is waiting. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. Go in the strength of the Lord, knowing that you are never alone.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ’s presence, we pray to the Lord.
For all who carry the weight of grief, that God may console them with His presence, strengthen them with His hope, and hold them in His everlasting love, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
On this mountain the LORD of hosts
will provide for all peoples
a feast of rich food and choice wines,
juicy, rich food and pure, choice wines.
On this mountain he will destroy
the veil that veils all peoples,
the web that is woven over all nations;
he will destroy death forever.
The Lord GOD will wipe away
the tears from every face;
the reproach of his people he will remove
from the whole earth; for the LORD has spoken.
On that day it will be said:
"Behold our God, to whom we looked to save us!
This is the LORD for whom we looked;
let us rejoice and be glad that he has saved us!"
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (6cd) I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
In verdant pastures he gives me repose;
beside restful waters he leads me;
he refreshes my soul.
R. I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
He guides me in right paths
for his name's sake.
Even though I walk in the dark valley
I fear no evil; for you are at my side
with your rod and your staff
that give me courage.
R. I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
You spread the table before me
in the sight of my foes;
you anoint my head with oil;
my cup overflows.
R. I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
Only goodness and kindness follow me
all the days of my life;
and I shall dwell in the house of the LORD
for years to come.
R. I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
I know how to live in humble circumstances;
I know also how to live with abundance.
In every circumstance and in all things
I have learned the secret of being well fed and of going hungry,
of living in abundance and of being in need. 
I can do all things in him who strengthens me. 
Still, it was kind of you to share in my distress.

My God will fully supply whatever you need,
in accord with his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
To our God and Father, glory forever and ever. Amen.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus again in reply spoke to the chief priests and elders of the people 
in parables, saying, 
"The kingdom of heaven may be likened to a king
who gave a wedding feast for his son. 
He dispatched his servants
to summon the invited guests to the feast,
but they refused to come.
A second time he sent other servants, saying,
'Tell those invited: "Behold, I have prepared my banquet,
my calves and fattened cattle are killed,
and everything is ready; come to the feast."'
Some ignored the invitation and went away,
one to his farm, another to his business. 
The rest laid hold of his servants,
mistreated them, and killed them. 
The king was enraged and sent his troops,
destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. 
Then he said to his servants, 'The feast is ready,
but those who were invited were not worthy to come. 
Go out, therefore, into the main roads
and invite to the feast whomever you find.'
The servants went out into the streets
and gathered all they found, bad and good alike,
and the hall was filled with guests. 
But when the king came in to meet the guests,
he saw a man there not dressed in a wedding garment. 
The king said to him, 'My friend, how is it
that you came in here without a wedding garment?'
But he was reduced to silence.
Then the king said to his attendants, 'Bind his hands and feet,
and cast him into the darkness outside,
where there will be wailing and grinding of teeth.'
Many are invited, but few are chosen."

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
